Crimea Installs Landline Payphones as Mobile Blackouts Persist — Russian occupation authorities in Crimea have begun installing public payphones after scheduled mobile network shutoffs and Ukrainian strikes left residents without communication. The devices reportedly work even without electricity and connect free of charge to emergency services.

Syrsky Breaks Silence, Apologizes to Ousted Defense Minister Fedorov — Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) Oleksandr Syrsky apologized to former Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov, saying he only learned of their conflict after it became public. Fedorov's dismissal last week has sparked protests since, renewing questions about President Volodymyr Zelensky’s military command.

Zelensky, UK’s Burnham to Discuss Anti-Ballistic Coalition Cooperation at Upcoming Meeting — President Volodymyr Zelensky spoke with the UK’s new prime minister, Andy Burnham, thanking him for continued support for Ukraine. Both agreed to meet soon to discuss expanding cooperation, including within the Anti-Ballistic Coalition.

Russian Strike Hits Civilian Enterprise in Odesa, Kills 6, Wounds 6 — A Russian strike on a civilian enterprise in the Odesa region killed six people and injured another six, with the attack sparking fires and damaging a gas pipeline. Rescue operations were still underway.

Russian Strikes on Dnipropetrovsk Region Kill 2, Injure 17, Including Children — Russian armed forces struck four districts of the Dnipropetrovsk region nearly 40 times on Monday, killing two people and injuring 17, including children as young as 1 year old. Residential apartments and other civilian infrastructure were damaged across multiple communities.

Lockheed Martin Unveils Cheaper Patriot Interceptor, PAC-3 ACE — As global demands surge, Lockheed Martin introduced the PAC-3 ACE, a Patriot interceptor designed to deter air and missile threats at less than half the cost of the PAC-3 MSE. The launch comes as Ukraine faces critical shortages of ballistic missile defense.

IN PHOTOS: What Are Ukrainians Saying About Fedorov’s Dismissal? — As protests against Fedorov’s dismissal continued nationwide over the weekend, the messages on protesters’ placards offered a not-so-subtle indication of what Ukrainians want – and, more subtly, how they believe the war for the country’s survival should be fought as it enters its fifth year.

Ukraine’s Game of Drones — The removal of Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov triggered criticism at home and abroad, with supporters crediting him for Ukraine’s wartime technological advances. However, Ukraine’s dominance in drone warfare will continue under newly appointed Defense Minister Yevhenii Khmara, a security and drone operations specialist.

Budanov Says Public ‘Heard’ as Zelensky Holds Marathon Talks With Ukraine's Top Commanders — Budanov said public concerns over Fedorov's dismissal had been heard and urged calm as Zelensky held another round of meetings with Ukraine's top military commanders. The consultations come amid continued protests and speculation over changes in the military leadership.

Ukraine's Next Drone Weapon Is a Boat That Launches FPV Swarms — Ukraine's Omega Special Purpose Center has developed a new unmanned boat capable of launching FPV drones, supporting combat divers, and intercepting aerial threats. The platform is designed to extend strike range and strengthen Ukraine's growing fleet of naval unmanned systems.

Withering, Relentless Ukraine Drone Strike Campaign Hits Crimea Hard — Ukraine’s drone forces have spent the past two weeks hammering Russian logistics networks supporting occupied Crimea, targeting fuel tankers, cargo ships, ferries, power infrastructure, rail hubs, bridges, and freight traffic. The operation is aimed at isolating Crimea from mainland Russia and degrading its value as a military base.

Russia Struggles to Staff New Drone Force as Military Recruitment Falters – Report — Russia has failed to recruit the planned number of personnel for its new Unmanned Systems Forces, with only 8,000 specialists trained by mid-2026 instead of the expected 34,400, according to CIT. The shortfall comes as Russia faces a broader slowdown in military recruitment.

Russia Uses More Jet-Powered Drones, S8000 Banderol Missiles in Latest Attacks — The spokesperson of the Ukrainian Air Force said Russia has increasingly relied on its jet-powered drones and the S8000 Banderol missiles in its barrage against Ukraine, with previous reports suggesting the Banderol to be largely a product of foreign-supplied components.

Ukraine Opens New Front in Drone Warfare With Sea-Launched FPV Strike — Ukraine's marines used Barracuda drone boats to launch FPV drones against Russian positions near occupied Zaliznyi Port. Despite losing one USV to four Lancet strikes, the mission successfully hit Russian troops, equipment, and logistics.

Has Life Been Found on Mars? — Life on Mars is almost a certainty, argues biologist Steve Benner, whose new book challenges decades of NASA orthodoxy. Re‑examining Viking mission data, he shows the landers’ life‑detection experiments were positive and that later discoveries undermine earlier dismissals. Could it be that life on Earth did not originate here after all?

Seven PMs Since January 2016: Britain’s Decade of ‘Chaos’ — Andy Burnham is set to become Britain’s seventh prime minister since 2016 after Keir Starmer resigned following plunging approval ratings and mounting pressure within Labour. Burnham takes office pledging to restore political stability after a decade marked by rapid leadership turnover under both major parties.

Ukraine Targets Russian Online Retailer — Ukrainian drone strikes on Wildberries logistics centers in Russia, which reportedly killed eight people, have sparked debate over their legitimacy. Supporters argue the facilities have military value because they supply dual-use goods, while critics say the attacks mainly harm small businesses and civilians, who bear the economic costs of the war.

Trump Pushes for Iran's Inclusion in Graham’s Sanctions Bill — Trump had called on the US Congress to include Iran-related provisions in the Sanction Russia Act in honor of late US Republican Senator Lindsey Graham, who championed the bill. However, the bill’s co-sponsor, Democratic Senator Richard Blumenthal, argued that reopening it risks delay and suggested the provisions be introduced via other bills instead.

Vamos, España! Such Football is Needed by the World — The victory of the Spanish national team in the World Cup final against Argentina became a triumph of playing philosophy over pragmatic calculation. Luis De la Fuente built a system where intensive pressing, compactness, and an analytical approach completely neutralize the opponent. The Spaniards revived true football of intellect, and the absolute advantage in the decisive match proved that Luis de la Fuente's coaching ideas are unsurpassed.

Ukraine’s Overnight Drone Campaign Extends Beyond Moscow to Crimea, Air Base, Shadow Fleet — Ukraine said its overnight drone campaign extended far beyond the Moscow region, targeting a key Russian military air base, air defense systems, Crimea’s energy infrastructure, and seven vessels, including three shadow fleet tankers, in the Black and Azov seas. Russia claimed it intercepted 381 Ukrainian drones.

Russian Strike on Turkish Cargo Ship Leaving Odesa Kills 10 — A Russian missile struck the Turkish-owned cargo ship Golden Leo as it departed Odesa with grain, killing 10 people. Ukraine says the attack targeted civilian shipping and comes amid an intensifying campaign against Black Sea ports and maritime exports.

The Follies of Historical Memory: Poland, Ukraine and the Politics of Selective Remembrance — Bohdan Vitvitsky argues that recent criticism from Polish politicians over Ukraine’s commemoration of the Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA) risks damaging relations at a time when both countries share vital security interests. Vitvitsky criticizes attempts by Polish politicians and the European Parliament to use historical grievances as political tools, arguing that such disputes benefit Russian propaganda

Russia Fires More Ballistic Missiles in 19 Days Than It Produces in a Month – Analysis — Russia launched 107 ballistic missiles and 20 Zircon missiles in the first 19 days of July, exceeding its estimated monthly ballistic missile production and using two-thirds of its planned annual Zircon output, according to Militarnyi, citing Ukrainian military data and military intelligence estimates.

Russian Anti-War Politician Ends Political Campaign After Pressure from Kremlin — Russian opposition politician Boris Nadezhdin has withdrawn from the September State Duma election after authorities blocked his campaign, labeled him a “foreign agent,” fined him over alleged extremist symbols, and restricted his movements. Nadezhdin said mounting pressure made it impossible to continue legally without putting his supporters, campaign team, and family at risk.

Farnborough 2026: Drones, Fighter Jets and Sovereignty — The Farnborough Airshow opens Monday with a strong focus on European rearmament, next-generation fighter jets, drones, and defense autonomy. Ukraine will showcase its battlefield-tested drone technologies, while Boeing seeks to restore confidence and highlight its MQ-28 Ghost Bat autonomous combat drone alongside delayed commercial aircraft programs.

Ukraine’s Massive 400-Drone Raid Hits Moscow Region Logistics Network, Fuel Sites — More than 400 drones targeted the Moscow region overnight, according to Russian officials, as Ukraine struck logistics hubs, an oil depot, and a residential building. The attack marked the second reported strike on a Wildberries warehouse in three days.

Georgian Legion Commander: From Russian Captivity to Fighting His Captors — Mamuka Mamulashvili, commander of the Georgian Legion, talks to Kyiv Post about why Georgian volunteers have been fighting alongside Ukraine since 2014, the long-standing ties between the two nations, Georgia’s own experience of resisting Russian aggression, and how the Russians held him in captivity when he was a child.

Zelensky to Hold ‘Key Talks’ on Strategy to End War Monday — President Volodymyr Zelensky announced in his Sunday evening address that he expects to hold “key conversations” on Monday regarding the strategy to conclude the war on acceptable terms. The announcement follows a weekend of extensive consultations with experienced military commanders, including Mykhailo Drapatyi, Volodymyr Horbatiuk, and Oleh Apostol, to assess battlefield conditions and future operations.

Estonian Foreign Minister Calls for Deeper Sanctions Against Russia — Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna has called for intensified pressure and tougher sanctions against Russia following a massive overnight ballistic missile attack on Kyiv. Tsahkna stated that “Moscow resorts to terror when it knows strategic gains through other means are slipping out of reach” and argued that continuous strategic isolation is necessary to halt the campaign. Polish Authorities Investigate Assault on Ukrainian Teenager for Speaking Native Language — A district prosecutor’s office in Płock, Poland, has launched an investigation into the physical and verbal assault of a 15-year-old Ukrainian boy who was attacked by an adult male on a city bus for speaking Ukrainian. The assailant reportedly struck the teenager and forced him and a companion off the vehicle.

Foreign Engineers for Ukraine: A Strategy for Victory? — Ukraine’s defense industry is producing military technology at an unprecedented pace, but a shortage of engineers and technical specialists is emerging as a major challenge. Attracting foreign talent could help increase production, accelerate innovation, strengthen knowledge transfer, and reinforce Ukraine’s position as a leader in defense technology.

Sanctions Busting? FIFA May pay World Cup Money to Russian Clubs — FIFA is planning to disburse a record $355 million through its Club Benefits Program following the 2026 World Cup. However, the organization faces potential legal action for reimbursing Russian clubs linked to sanctioned entities, such as Lukoil-owned Spartak Moscow. An investigation by the journalism platform Follow the Money revealed that FIFA previously paid $1.2 million to six Russian clubs after the 2022 tournament, potentia

Satellite Imagery Confirms Destruction of Russian Tu-95 Bomber at Engels Airbase — Satellite images from Planet Labs, published by the investigative project Schemes on July 19, confirm the destruction of a Russian Tu-95 strategic bomber at the Engels-2 military airbase in the Saratov region. The imagery shows the aircraft effectively severed in half, corroborating statements made by the Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) regarding a long-range drone strike on July 17.

Russian Ballistic Missile Strike Destroys UKRTAC Military Gear Factory in Kyiv — A direct Russian missile strike completely destroyed the manufacturing facilities and warehouses of UKRTAC, a Ukrainian producer of military gear and personal protective equipment, during an attack on Kyiv on Sunday, July 19. Company founder Severion Dangadze confirmed the total destruction of the plant but reported no casualties among the staff. The strike occurred during a barrage involving approximately 40 ballis

Ukraine’s Children Are Rebuilding Their Futures Far From Home – We Must Not Fail Them Now — Ukrainian children displaced by Russia’s invasion are rebuilding their lives while carrying trauma, disrupted schooling and the struggle to preserve their language. Community schools like St Mary’s in London support more than 2,500 children, offering stability and cultural continuity, yet full‑time trauma‑focused provision still lacks funding. With no recognised Ukrainian‑language qualification in the UK,

Moldova to Acquire Drone Interception Systems with EU Funding — Moldova’s Ministry of Defense will purchase new drone detection and interception systems backed by a €120 million ($137 million) EU assistance package. State Secretary of the Moldovan Ministry of Foreign Affairs Valeriu Mija stated that the country’s airspace has been violated 34 times by drones and missiles since the start of Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

US Completes Eighth Night of Strikes Against Iranian Military Facilities — US Central Command (CENTCOM) confirmed early Sunday that American forces completed an eighth consecutive night of strikes against Iranian military targets. The operations hit coastal surveillance and air defense facilities, maritime assets, and missile and drone storage sites. US forces also targeted elements of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) responsible for a July 17 attack on US personnel in Jordan.

Russian Strike on Kharkiv Suburbs Kills Three, Injures 20 — Russian forces attacked the suburbs of Kharkiv on Sunday, July 19, resulting in three civilian deaths and 20 people injured. Kharkiv Regional Military Administration Head Oleh Syniehubov reported that nine individuals were hospitalized, with three in serious condition. The Polish Interior Ministry stated that border officers intercepted all attempts this year. The Challenges Facing UK’s Next PM Andy Burnham — Former Greater Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham is scheduled to become the UK’s seventh prime minister in a decade next week following the resignation of Sir Keir Starmer. Burnham inherits a challenging domestic and international agenda as he takes the helm of the Labour Party. SBU Drones Strike Three Oil Depots in Russia’s Stavropol Region and Shadow Fleet Tanker — The Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) claimed responsibility for drone strikes that ignited massive fires at three oil depots in Russia’s Stavropol region on Sunday. SBU maritime drones also struck the Avero, a Suezmax-class shadow fleet tanker used to transport Russian crude oil to Asia in violation of international sanctions. Kyiv Protests Grow: Calls to Reinstate Fedorov and Oust Ukraine’s Commander-in-Chief — Protests in Kyiv on Saturday, July 18, have expanded from calls to reinstate former Minister of Defense Mykhailo Fedorov to demands for the dismissal of Ukraine’s Commander-in-Chief, General Oleksandr Syrskyi. Protesters accuse Syrsky of obstructing military reforms and hindering the advancement of younger officers – allegations that gained momentum following Fedorov’s public criticism.

Hungarian President Sulyok Signs Constitutional Amendment Ending His Term Prematurely — Hungarian President Tamás Sulyok reluctantly signed a constitutional amendment on Saturday, July 18, that prematurely terminates his mandate. Ukrainian Railways (Ukrzaliznytsia) reported that a monitor group issued an early evacuation order, helping to prevent mass casualties, though one conductor sustained light injuries. Passengers were transferred to Zaporizhzhia via buses coordinated by the regional military administration.

Putin’s Ukraine Failure Could Speed Russia’s Breakup, Historian Says — British-Polish historian Norman Davies stated that Vladimir Putin’s attempts to reconstruct the Russian Empire have failed, exposing military weaknesses and reducing Moscow to a vassal state dependent on Beijing. We Joined a Secret Ukrainian Robot Mission to the Front Line — Kyiv Post joined a Ukrainian UGV unit from the 13th Khartiia Brigade on a mission to deliver food and ammunition to front-line positions under the threat of Russian drones.
These unmanned ground vehicles can travel dozens of kilometers, evacuate wounded soldiers and retrieve damaged drones. One of them, nicknamed “Erdogan,” continued operating even after hitting a mine and being struck by an FPV drone.

Ukraine’s Watershed — Donald Trump used this month’s NATO Summit to posture but ultimately backed two major moves: a strike against Iran and long‑delayed Patriot missiles for Ukraine, which faces relentless Russian ballistic attacks. Let’s not forget – Europe’s decades of under‑militarization enabled Russia’s invasion, but Trump’s pressure has finally forced NATO states to strengthen defenses. How the Brother of Ukraine’s Top Investigator Came to Own 143 Apartments — An investigative report published by several Ukrainian media outlets as part of the "Initiative 143" alleges that Oleksandr Sukhachov, the brother of State Bureau of Investigation (DBR) Director Oleksii Sukhachov, acquired 143 real estate properties in Kharkiv between 2018 and 2020 at prices below market value, some for as little as $932-1,856 – per apartment, not per square meter.

Sanctioned Russian Shadow Fleet Tanker Spills Oil Near Oman Coast — Satellite imagery indicates that the Caroline Bezengi, a sanctioned Russian shadow fleet tanker, is spilling oil in a marine conservation area off the coast of Oman. The vessel, which loaded oil in Novorossiysk, last transmitted its position on June 11. Finland Restricts Maritime and Air Traffic in Gulf of Finland Over Drone Threat — On July 18, Finland temporarily suspended maritime and air traffic in the eastern Gulf of Finland due to potential drone threats. The Finnish Defense Forces stated that the restrictions, which lasted from 5:45 a.m. to approximately 9:00 a.m. local time, were a preventative measure to ensure civilian safety and prepare for possible drone interceptions. No drones crossed into Finnish territory.

Russian Jet-Powered Drone Strike on Kryvyi Rih Kills 1 Civilian — On Saturday, July 18, a Russian jet-powered Shahed drone struck a critical infrastructure facility in Kryvyi Rih, Dnipropetrovsk region, killing one civilian and injuring others. The strike ignited a fire and prompted an emergency response. This attack occurred amid a broader wave of Russian strikes across southern and central Ukraine on July 17-18.

Ukraine’s Long-Range Sanctions Need Europe’s Support — With Europe consistently reluctant to implement tougher sanctions on Russian oil, Ukraine has taken matters into its own hands and launched its own long-range sanctions against the industry that literally fuels Russia’s war machine.

Russia Plans to Mobilize 500,000 Personnel by Autumn, Prepares for New Fronts — Russia is preparing an autumn mobilization of 500,000 personnel, according to Andriy Kovalenko, head of Ukraine’s Center for Countering Disinformation. Kovalenko stated that some conscripts will be sent to the eastern front within two weeks to address personnel shortages, while others will undergo a month of training to potentially open a new front. CIA Director Says AI Drones Reduce Russian Recruits’ Battlefield Lifespan to Minutes — CIA Director John Ratcliffe reported that Ukrainian artificial intelligence-guided drones have reduced the average battlefield survival time of new Russian recruits to 20-30 minutes. Speaking at a defense summit, Ratcliffe noted these cost-effective systems help Ukraine counter Russia’s manpower advantage, as US officials estimate Russian losses at 7,000 soldiers weekly.

Fedorov is emerging as a challenger to Zelensky | Bohdan Nahaylo — The dismissal of Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov has triggered public protests and exposed a divide between his technology-focused approach and the traditional methods of Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrsky. Kyiv Post Editor-in-Chief noted that President Volodymyr Zelensky’s decision to side with Syrsky has politically galvanized younger Ukrainians who view Fedorov as a reformer.

Schrödinger’s Elections — Russians are slated to go to the polls from Sept. 18 to 20, during which 450 seats of the Russian Federation’s State Duma will be decided. Whether or not real elections will take place has become an ontological problem akin to the Schrödinger cat paradox of quantum mechanics.

The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps threatened full-scale offensive operations if US strikes continue. US Central Command confirmed targeting Iranian logistics and naval assets.

China Declines to Supply Equipment for Russian Northern Sea Route Fleet — China has declined to supply propulsion and steering systems for Russia’s large-tonnage ice-class vessels due to international sanctions, hindering Moscow’s efforts to develop the Northern Sea Route. Russian shipyards lack the capacity and domestic equipment to build the required Arc7 ice-class tankers. A Senior Foreign Service member with over 30 years of diplomatic experience, Oudkirk previously served in roles at the US Department of Defense and as Director of the American Institute in Taiwan. She succeeds Julie Davis, who concluded her diplomatic mission as the acting head of the embassy in Ukraine on June 27.

Local authorities in the Tambov region reported the deaths of seven Wildberries employees.

Russian Strikes Target Odesa Port, UN Warehouse in Dnipro, Bus in Marhanets — On Friday, July 17, Russian forces conducted multiple strikes across Ukraine, targeting port infrastructure in the Odesa region, a UN World Food Programme warehouse in Dnipro, and a civilian bus in Marhanets.
